<p class="skill-reference-meta"><span>Arcantry 1.0.0</span><code>adopt-arcantry</code></p>

Adopt the smallest useful Arcantry boundary while preserving repository-owned tooling, knowledge sources, and private state.

## When to use

Inspect, adopt, validate, or remove Arcantry at shared, private, or configuration-free project scope while preserving repository-owned files.

## Link this skill

```text
arcantry skills link adopt-arcantry --scope user
```

The standard destination is `~/.agents/skills`. Codex reads this universal Agent Skills location directly.

### Claude compatibility

```text
arcantry skills link adopt-arcantry --scope user --compat claude
```

This keeps the universal link and adds a Claude alias to the same canonical package.

## Compatibility

Source kinds: `openspec`, `changelog`, `todo-txt`.

Adapters:

- `openspec`: `>=1 <2`
- `keep-a-changelog`: `>=1 <3`
- `todo-txt`: `>=1 <2`

## Learning outcomes

- Distinguish discovery, footprint, and management for each project source.
- Choose an explicit preservation or source transition boundary without automatic conversion.
- Keep local state private unless the default remote branch establishes a different repository policy.
- Prefer user-wide skills and make repository-private packages an explicit fallback.

## Examples

### Adopt Arcantry in a mature repository

**Prompt**

> Use the adopt-arcantry skill to inspect a mature repository and plan selective adoption while preserving existing tooling and knowledge sources.

**Expected outcome**

A source-by-source adoption plan that leaves project-owned files unchanged until explicitly applied.

### Diagnose an existing adoption

**Prompt**

> Use the adopt-arcantry skill to inspect and validate this repository without removing unknown files or changing external systems.

**Expected outcome**

A repository health report backed by Arcantry validation and doctor checks, with private state kept local.
